facts.text: Malta, Ohio, was founded in 1816 by ex‑sailor Simeon Pool, who named it after the Mediterranean island he once visited.
A 19th‑century stone jail, the Morgan County Dungeon, was rediscovered in 1964, moved to Main Street, and now bears an Ohio Historical Marker.
The village hosts two National Register‑listed wooden bridges: the 1867 Helmick Mill Covered Bridge and the nearby Adams Covered Bridge.
Malta grew along the Muskingum River, which became a key trade route after locks and dams were built between 1836 and 1841.
Every July, Malta partners with McConnelsville to stage Civil War Encampment Days, complete with reenactments and cannon fire.
Rock Hollow School, a one‑room building erected in 1877, still stands as a reminder of 19th‑century rural education.
